title: The threshold attack calibrates without using final evaluation membership labels

invariants.description: Re-running the attack with the evaluation ground truth permuted must give bit-identical released outputs, scores, thresholds, calibration and decisions, and the calibration and shadow populations must share no record with the victim's training set or the candidates.
No record may be duplicated or shared between the six populations (row-level SHA-256 check).
The threshold calibrated for FPR ≤ 1% on reference models must not exceed 3% FPR on the unseen evaluation non-members (observed 1/250 = 0.4%); an evaluation-optimal threshold is never used.
The balanced threshold chosen on calibration data alone must still classify ≥ 75% of evaluation candidates correctly (observed 404/500 = 80.8%).

rationale: Thresholds chosen on the evaluation ROC curve would overstate leakage. The attack's thresholds come only from reference models trained by the attacker on its own calibration population; this case checks that executably (ground-truth permutation) and that the calibrated operating point transfers.
